summary:
TerraTrend is an interactive tool that helps students and the public investigate environmental change using Earth science data. Users choose from 17 variables and select a location or region, then explore a long-term time series. The graph displays raw values or seasonal anomalies, a 12-month running mean, a trend line, and a 95% confidence band. TerraTrend calculates the rate and total amount of change and tests statistical significance using a linear-regression t-test and the Mann–Kendall test with Sen’s slope. Plain-language explanations, guided demos, comparisons, tailored resources, and Excel or CSV exports support further investigation.
Historical analyses use NASA POWER data based on MERRA-2 and satellite and land-model data accessed through NASA Giovanni. A separate WeatherAPI-powered card shows current local weather. By bringing data discovery, regional analysis, visualization, and statistical testing into one guided workflow, TerraTrend makes Earth science more accessible and helps users build data-literacy skills. Its impact is to help people move beyond headlines: they can investigate how environmental trends differ by place, judge the strength and uncertainty of evidence, and make more informed connections between scientific findings and the world around them.
details:
What It Does & How It Works

TerraTrend is an interactive web application that helps students and the public investigate environmental change using real Earth science data. Users select from 17 environmental variables, choose a point or region on an interactive Leaflet map, and explore multi-decade time series. The chart displays raw values or seasonal anomalies, a 12-month running mean, a linear trend line, and a 95% confidence band. Behind the scenes, TerraTrend calculates the rate and total amount of change and evaluates statistical significance using both a linear-regression t-test and the Mann–Kendall test (with Sen’s slope).

Historical analyses draw from NASA POWER (MERRA-2 reanalysis) and satellite and land-model datasets accessed via NASA Giovanni, while a separate WeatherAPI-powered card displays current local conditions for context. Users can also launch guided demos, compare regions or variables side by side, revisit past investigations via a session history bar, consult a Smart FAQ that explains the chart and statistical results in plain language, and export datasets to Excel or CSV.

Creativity, Benefits & Intended Impact

Rather than presenting raw climate tables or intimidating statistical outputs, TerraTrend creatively bridges scientific rigor and approachable design—turning data analysis into a guided, detective-style investigation. By pairing statistical tests with plain-language verdicts and clear explanations, it helps users see how climate trends differ across regions and grasp the uncertainty behind scientific conclusions. My goal is to strengthen data literacy and empower students and curious learners to move beyond headlines through evidence-based exploration.

Tools & Development Considerations

I developed TerraTrend independently on a laptop using Visual Studio Code, with Claude Code assisting with coding and debugging. The project uses Python, JavaScript, CSS, and HTML; its interactive map uses Leaflet. Throughout development, I prioritized the needs of high school and college students by designing a clear step-by-step workflow and transparent definitions. I also considered data coverage, seasonal cycles, natural year-to-year variability, and responsible science communication, so statistically inconclusive results are not presented as proof that no change is occurring.
